themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK versus a 2.6-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks (776% increase, z-score 12.32), suggesting a coordinated tagging campaign or removal service breakdown requiring immediate investigation into whether this reflects organized activity or municipal response failure.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
776% spike with z-score of 12.32 (statistically significant anomaly)
Represents 8x normal weekly baseline in a single week
reporting_angles: Are residents reporting the same tag/artist, or is this widespread? Interview 311 data to map locations.
Has the Department of Sanitation's graffiti removal crew been deployed to CD314, or are they backlogged?

themes_detail.label: Street noise surge in district
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks jumped to 84 THIS WEEK compared to 20.8 weekly average (305% increase, z-score 4.33), suggesting either a new noise source (construction, events, street activity) or a breakdown in enforcement that warrants on-ground verification.
evidence: 84 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 20.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
4x normal baseline suggests acute, not chronic, problem
reporting_angles: Canvass Flatbush Avenue and Ocean Parkway corridors to identify what's causing the noise—new construction, bar/venue activity, or traffic patterns.
Cross-reference with DOB permits filed (320 total in 90 days) to see if a major project just started.

themes_detail.label: Illegal posting infestation
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 6 LAST WEEK from a 0.2 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score 13.28)—the highest z-score in the data—indicating either a targeted poster campaign or a systemic permitting/enforcement gap requiring urgent door-knocking to identify the source and scope.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
2300% spike with z-score of 13.28 (highest statistical anomaly in entire dataset)
reporting_angles: Canvass poles, walls, and transit stops on Flatbush and Ocean Parkway to photograph and catalog what's being posted—is it political, commercial, or spam?
Interview Parks/Sanitation enforcement to determine if they're aware of the campaign and what removal capacity exists.

themes_detail.label: Air quality concerns emerge
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints rose to 4 THIS WEEK from a 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score 3.92), a small absolute volume but a significant spike that could signal poor air conditions or new pollution source coinciding with ongoing rezoning activity in the district.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Timing overlaps with active ULURP applications (1455 Coney Island Ave, 2586 Nostrand Ave rezoning) and 320 DOB permit filings in 90 days
reporting_angles: Determine if complaints are localized to specific blocks (near rezoning sites or construction) or citywide.
Cross-check air quality sensor data from DEP or EPA to verify if objective conditions support 311 spikes, or if it reflects subjective perception during construction.

themes_detail.label: Encampment uptick suggests homelessness shift
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 4.41), indicating a possible surge in unsheltered populations or a shift in street presence that may correlate with weather, shelter closures, or service gaps.
evidence: 5 encampment complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Data is 2 weeks old; requires verification of whether trend has persisted or receded
reporting_angles: Visit the locations where encampment complaints were filed to assess current conditions and speak with unhoused residents about what brought them to CD314.
Interview NYC Department of Homeless Services to understand shelter capacity, recent closures, or service reductions in this district.
